The Austrian State Treaty, signed in Vienna on 15 May 1955 by the four occupying powers, restored Austria as a free, independent and democratic state.

After 1945 Austria, like Germany, was divided into American, British, French and Soviet zones, with Vienna under joint control. Unlike Germany, it had one government for the whole country. After Stalin's death the Soviet Union agreed to withdraw, once Austria promised neutrality.

The last troops left in autumn 1955, and on 26 October, now the national day, parliament declared permanent neutrality. Austria stayed outside NATO and became a meeting place between East and West during the Cold War, with Vienna hosting UN agencies and OPEC. It ended the occupation that followed the Anschluss. See Austria.
sum: The Austrian State Treaty, signed in Vienna on 15 May 1955 by the four occupying powers, restored Austria as a free, independent and democratic state.
